title: Roofr | Roofing scheduling software explained
summary: Roofing scheduling software keeps every job on one calendar that office and crews can both see. Learn how and why it's a roofing contractor's best friend.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Roofing scheduling software keeps every job on one calendar that your office and crews can both see. When a date changes, a crew lead sees it on their phone instead of waiting for a call. For a roofing business, the best place for it is your roofing job management software, next to your estimates and invoices.


When you're running one crew, a whiteboard in the shop and a group text to your crew lead are enough to track who's going where. With a second or third crew, that setup can start missing jobs. A job makes it onto the board but not into the group text. Other times, the lead on that job hears about a change from a coworker in the driveway.


Roofing scheduling software puts it all in one place.


## What does roofing scheduling software do?


Roofing scheduling software trades the whiteboard for a calendar that shows which crew is on each job and the day it starts. When you pair it with job boards, it also shows where each project stands between the signed contract and the final invoice.


Seeing the whole week on one screen lets your office manager spot an idle crew or an overbooked day. You can add your sales reps' appointments too, so you know which rep is free for an inspection without calling around.


Because everyone works from the same calendar, your office only has to make the change once. If rain pushes Tuesday's tear-off to Thursday, the office moves the job. The crew lead sees the new date before they load the truck.


## What problems does roofing scheduling software solve?


Once you have more jobs sold than crews to start them, you need to know which signed jobs have waited the longest.[Roofing Contractor's 2026 Homeowner Survey](https://www.roofingcontractor.com/articles/101716-5-things-roofing-contractors-want-to-know-about-rcs-2026-homeowner-survey) found most homeowners expect work to start within two weeks of accepting a quote, with a typical wait of 3 to 13 days.


On a whiteboard, a job you closed 10 days ago looks the same as one you closed yesterday unless someone writes the date next to it. Scheduling software puts every job that still needs a crew in one column on a job board. That dashboard can then show how long each one has been sitting there.


When a homeowner asks how soon you can start, a rep on a sales call can't see the whiteboard back at the shop. If the rep has access to the job board, they can give a date based on the jobs already in line.


Go through that board each morning to see what's holding each job up, like a permit or a material delivery. When the date the rep gave won't work out, tell the homeowner before they have to ask. Roofr's[2026 Homeowner Report](https://roofr.com/masterclass/what-do-homeowners-want-from-roofers) found that 74% of homeowners rank responsiveness and communication above price. A quick update helps protect the job you already sold.


If keeping the whiteboard current takes more of your office's time than planning next week's jobs, you've outgrown it.


## What should you look for in roofing scheduling software?


One of the most important things to look for is roofing scheduling software that works with the system your office already uses. If everyone books appointments in Google Calendar, you'll want two-way sync, so a change in either calendar shows up in the other.


Without it, someone has to re-enter everything you book in Google. Which is exactly the kind of busywork you're buying software to get rid of.


Past that, a good tool should cover the roofing side of the job, which a generic calendar can’t handle. Look for one where:


- Delivery dates belong on the same job as the crew's start date, so nobody has to check two places.
- Subs need to appear on the schedule right alongside your own crews.
- Moving a job to the next stage can trigger a task automatically, like creating a material order once the homeowner signs.
- Once a job wraps up, job costing shows how its estimate compares with what it actually cost.


If your crew leads check the schedule from their phones, test the mobile view before you sign up. Have one of them pull up tomorrow's job, then see how quickly they find the address and start time. If it takes more than a few taps, expect them to keep calling the office instead.

## Should scheduling live inside your roofing job management software?


For most replacement contractors, scheduling works best inside your[roofing job management software](https://roofr.com/blog/crm-for-roofers-everything-you-need-to-know) . The measurements, proposal, and payments all live there, so the start date belongs with them.


If your calendar sits in a separate app, someone on your team has to retype every signed or moved job by hand. Miss one change, and the office ends up with a different start date than the crew.


A standalone scheduling tool can still make sense for a large repair department routing several short stops a day. For crews that spend a day or more on a roof, a separate app just adds another login, more maintenance, and its own monthly bill.


That's the situation[Chase Caldwell of Homemasters](https://roofr.com/case-studies/homemasters) in Bend, Oregon, moved away from when he replaced three apps with Roofr. He now saves more than 15 hours a week, and as he put it, "I can focus on 1 app, instead of trying to manage 3 apps."

## **Frequently asked questions**


**What is roofing scheduling software?**


Roofing scheduling software is a tool that organizes your jobs, crews, and appointments on a shared calendar. That way you know what work is happening, who's on it, and when. It replaces a whiteboard with a single, real-time view everyone on the team can access.


**How is scheduling software different from a roofing CRM?**


A CRM manages your whole sales and job process. That covers leads, estimates, proposals, and payments. Scheduling is one piece of it: the calendar and crew side. If your crews mainly do replacement work, a CRM with a built-in calendar means you don't need a separate tool.


**Can I schedule roofing crews in Google Calendar?**


You can, but plain Google Calendar doesn't connect appointments to job details, crews, or customer records. A roofing tool that syncs with Google Calendar gives you the familiar Google view plus the job context. Roofr Calendar, for example, syncs both ways.


**How much does roofing scheduling software cost?**


It varies. Some tools charge per user, which costs more as your team grows. Roofr doesn't charge per seat. A calendar and job boards come with every plan, starting with the free Starter plan. Scale adds more boards, crew management, job costing, and the full performance dashboard. Always confirm current pricing before you commit.


**What's the best way to schedule roofing jobs without missing start dates?**


Get every signed job onto your job board as soon as you win it, even if the start is still weeks out. Once the homeowner picks a color and the permit comes through, assign the crew, then set automatic reminders for upcoming starts. Keeping scheduling in the same system as your estimates and payments means nobody has to copy a job's dates from one tool to another.
